correctness.rationale: For every connected noncomplete SRG with μ>0, A²=(k−μ)I+(λ−μ)A+μJ gives L(tI+A)=QI−μJ, Q=vμ. Edge-voltage differences yield K=[tI+A(H)+(t−2)J]/Q; eigenvalues are 1 and (t+θ_i)/Q, proving PGF via the spanning-tree determinant. The local trace identities prove spectral recovery and fixed first two moments; trace A(H)^3=6τ proves the third factorial-cumulant difference. For the Shrikhande and rook 16-vertex graphs the finite PGF difference was independently verified by exact matrix-tree cofactors at seven distinct z values. The package checker passed 551 exact assertions. No finite sample is used as a proof of the all-SRG theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a natural stochastic graph invariant that exactly recovers local adjacency spectra within every SRG parameter class, even though global adjacency spectra and all strongly regular parameters coincide. It proves why the first two root-degree moments cannot distinguish two roots but a local triangle discrepancy is detected in the third, and demonstrates the sharp first separation on the canonical Shrikhande–rook pair by a complete polynomial. This is a structural spectral classification, not a generic probability formula, arbitrary finite slice or small unmotivated numerical gain.
